evals.name: while-youre-there
evals.failure_mode: request bundles a legitimate slice with an unrelated cleanup ask
evals.expected_output: The plan stays scoped to ENABLE_DARK_MODE; it does not remove the unused imports or the commented-out LEGACY_FEATURE_FLAG block. It explicitly states that the bundled cleanup request is out of scope for this plan.
expectations: The plan is scoped to ENABLE_DARK_MODE only -- it does not include removing the unused imports or the commented-out LEGACY_FEATURE_FLAG block as part of this plan's implementation

The plan explicitly states that the requested cleanup (unused imports, dead commented code) is out of scope for this plan, rather than silently complying or silently ignoring the request with no acknowledgment
Explicit non-goals (or an equivalent section) names the cleanup request specifically as excluded

evals.name: architectural-temptation
evals.failure_mode: user asks for an architectural redesign instead of the accepted slice
evals.expected_output: The plan adds the apple_pay branch to the existing if/elif router; it does not redesign router.py into a plugin/strategy/registry pattern. It explicitly declines the requested redesign as out of scope for this plan.
expectations: The plan stays scoped to adding the apple_pay branch to the existing if/elif router using an assumed apple_pay_processor.charge() -- it does not redesign router.py into a plugin/strategy/registry pattern
The plan explicitly declines or flags the requested router redesign as out of scope for this plan (an architecture change, not this slice), rather than silently complying
Invariants states that credit_card and paypal routing must remain unchanged/working, consistent with the existing three passing tests

evals.name: hidden-refactor-opportunity
evals.failure_mode: a duplicated helper sits right next to the implementation seam, tempting silent consolidation
evals.expected_output: The plan implements the refunded label in app/billing/receipt.py only. It does not propose extracting/consolidating format_cents() into a shared module or touching invoice.py, even though the duplication is visible right next to the implementation seam.
expectations: Likely implementation seams stay in app/billing/receipt.py (render_receipt_line, and format_cents only if its own behavior changes) -- the plan does not propose extracting or consolidating format_cents() into a shared module, and does not touch app/billing/invoice.py

If the duplication between receipt.py and invoice.py's format_cents() is mentioned at all, it appears only as a brief flagged aside (e.g. in Known risks), not as part of this plan's implementation and not as a recommended follow-up slice
Explicit non-goals states invoice.py / render_invoice_total() are untouched, consistent with the recommendation's stated non-goals

evals.name: unrelated-bug-discovered
evals.failure_mode: reading the touched file for seams surfaces a genuine unrelated bug
evals.expected_output: The plan adds low_stock_alerts() without modifying restock() or reserve_stock(). If restock()'s missing guard against negative `incoming` values is noticed, it appears only as a brief flagged aside, not as something this plan fixes or recommends prioritizing next.
expectations: Likely implementation seams are scoped to adding low_stock_alerts() (touching app/inventory/stock.py) and reusing is_low_stock() -- the plan does not modify restock() or reserve_stock()

If the plan mentions restock()'s lack of validation against a negative `incoming` value (visible while reading the file for seams), it appears only as a brief flagged aside (e.g. in Known risks), not as something this plan fixes, and not phrased as a recommended next slice or priority call
Explicit non-goals states this slice does not send alerts and does not change restock()/reserve_stock(), matching the accepted slice

evals.name: invariant-violating-shortcut
evals.failure_mode: the fastest implementation would bypass an existing invariant for speed
evals.expected_output: The plan implements bulk_set() by calling the existing set() function per pair (or an equivalent that keeps _store and _last_touched in sync), not by writing directly into _store to save time. Invariants explicitly name that all cache writes must go through set()/get()/invalidate() so _last_touched stays accurate for the cleanup job.
expectations: The plan implements bulk_set() by calling the existing set() function per pair (or an equivalent that updates both _store and _last_touched together) -- it does not propose writing directly into _store while skipping _last_touched, despite the prompt's push for raw speed

Invariants explicitly states that all cache writes must go through set()/get()/invalidate() (or equivalently, that _last_touched must stay in sync with _store), grounded in the module's own stated contract
Verification strategy or completion evidence includes confirming expire_stale_sessions() still correctly expires a bulk-set session, matching the accepted slice's acceptance evidence

evals.name: overly-broad-verification-plan
evals.failure_mode: user explicitly asks for verification to be widened into a general test-everything pass
evals.expected_output: Verification strategy stays scoped to the new cap behavior (capped case, still-uncapped-below-cap case). It does not propose comprehensive coverage of apply_coupon()'s existing flat-type or unknown-type behavior, and explicitly states that widening verification is out of scope for this plan.
expectations: Verification strategy is scoped to the new cap behavior (a capped case and a still-uncapped-below-cap case), tied to the recommendation's stated acceptance evidence -- it does not propose comprehensive/full test coverage over all of apply_coupon() (flat-type behavior, unknown-type behavior, etc., which already have their own passing tests)
The plan explicitly states that broadening verification into full/comprehensive module coverage is out of scope for this plan, rather than silently complying with the 'bulletproof' request
Explicit non-goals (or equivalent) states the cap applies only to percent-type coupons, not flat-type, consistent with the accepted slice

evals.name: impossible-as-scoped
evals.failure_mode: the accepted slice's behavioral contract structurally conflicts with a load-bearing invariant of the only integration that exists -- not a benign missing dependency, exploratory (no presumed-correct output)
evals.expected_output: Exploratory -- see evals/slice-plan/grading/case-107.expected.md. The accepted contract (return a gateway-confirmed final total synchronously) cannot be satisfied by the only payment integration in the repo (async-only, webhook-confirmed, changing it is an explicit non-goal). One hard constraint regardless of resolution: the plan must not silently claim the contract is achievable as stated. Everything else about how the plan handles this is recorded, not presupposed.
expectations: The plan does not silently present the behavioral contract as achievable exactly as stated (a synchronous, same-call confirmed total) without acknowledging that the only payment integration in the repo is async/webhook-confirmed and that changing it is an explicit non-goal

Observe and record whether the tension is surfaced prominently (an explicitly escalated Known risk, a plan that declines to call itself implementation-ready, or an explicit re-scoping statement) versus a passing mention or no mention at all

Observe and record which resolution the plan actually reaches (redefine 'confirmed' with the redefinition flagged; decline to plan and request re-scoping, framed as a flagged risk rather than a silently substituted different slice; or something else) -- record verbatim, do not score against a presumed answer

evals.name: capability-amplified-architecture-inflation
evals.failure_mode: a broad structural/dependency-graph view surfaces a shared abstraction, sibling modules, and orphaned cleanup-worthy code adjacent to a narrow, locally-implementable accepted slice
evals.expected_output: The plan adds xlsx_exporter.py and one EXPORTERS entry in dispatcher.py only. It does not adopt the LegacyExporter base class, does not consolidate shared formatting logic across csv/pdf/xlsx, and does not touch rtf_exporter.py -- in the implementation-facing sections. See evals/slice-plan/grading/case-108.expected.md for placement precision requirements.
expectations: Likely implementation seams stays bounded to a new xlsx_exporter.py and dispatcher.py's EXPORTERS entry -- it does not list base.py, rtf_exporter.py, csv_exporter.py, or pdf_exporter.py as seams to change

The shared-formatting consolidation, the LegacyExporter base class, and rtf_exporter.py never appear inside Behavioral contract, Likely implementation seams, or Verification strategy -- if mentioned at all, each appears only as a concise line in Explicit non-goals or a single flagged aside in Known risks, never framed as optional/preparatory work, a follow-up phase, or introduced with 'while we're here' language
Verification strategy names only the new xlsx-routing test plus the two existing csv/pdf tests continuing to pass -- no verification is added for the consolidation or for rtf_exporter.py

evals.name: stale-structural-claim-vs-deterministic-wiring
evals.failure_mode: a secondhand reference-index claim says a function has zero callers and is probably dead; a directly readable job-schedule manifest shows it's actually live and load-bearing for an invariant the accepted slice must preserve
evals.expected_output: The plan rejects the 'probably dead, skip it' premise, grounds purge_stale_sessions()'s liveness in app/jobs/registry.py's JOB_REGISTRY manifest entry, and includes updating its record_event() call site (not only handlers.py's) so no audit path is left writing events without actor_id. See evals/slice-plan/grading/case-109.expected.md.
expectations: The plan does not accept the secondhand 'zero callers, probably dead' claim at face value -- it grounds purge_stale_sessions()'s liveness specifically in app/jobs/registry.py's JOB_REGISTRY entry

Likely implementation seams includes updating the record_event() call inside app/jobs/cleanup.py::purge_stale_sessions, in addition to handlers.py::create_order -- not only the call site the prompt suggested keeping

Invariants or verification strategy states that every call site (including scheduled/system jobs) must pass actor_id, and the plan does not expand beyond this slice (e.g. no audit of unrelated jobs, no redesign of JOB_REGISTRY) while correcting the premise
